photos.desc: Skin of the African albino frog Xenopus laevis
African clawed frog ( Xenopus laevis , also known as the platanna ) in Grant Museum of Zoology, London, England.
Captive male albino clawed frog in typical floating position with just the eyes and nose sticking out. Note the black forearms used to hold onto females during amplexus.

These plancton feeding larvae of the clawed frog (probably Xenopus laevis ) are social living creatures. The tentacles give them a catfish like appearance. Taken in Munda Wanga Botanical Garden, Lusak
